conversations.prompt: How can I become a better writer?
conversations.chosen_response:

• Read as much as you can. Read good literature, both classic and contemporary. Also, read the newspaper, good magazines, and essays and articles by writers you admire. Reading good literature will improve your vocabulary and sentence structure. It will also improve your ability to express your ideas in clear, well-crafted sentences. Reading contemporary literature will make you aware of the latest trends in writing.

• Set aside time every day to write. If you can only set aside half an hour a day, that’s better than nothing. At the very least, set aside 15 minutes a day to write. Also, set aside one day a week to work on your writing project without any interruptions. This will force you to concentrate, and it will improve your discipline.

• Always read your work aloud. Reading your work aloud will help you spot grammatical and structural errors. It will also help you identify awkward sentences and vague or ambiguous passages.

• Have someone else read your work. If you have a friend who’s also a writer, have him or her read your work. Ask your friend to point out any weaknesses in your writing and offer suggestions for improvement. If you don’t have a writing friend, ask a teacher or another educated person to read your work. Most people are willing to help a writer in need.

• Don’t give up. Writing isn’t easy, and nobody becomes a good writer overnight. With patience and perseverance, however, you can develop into a good writer.
